hospital_course: You came in with 4 days of fever, cough with yellow sputum, and shortness of breath. A chest X-ray showed pneumonia in the right lower lobe. You received IV antibiotics and oxygen, and your breathing and oxygen level are now back to normal on room air.

medications.name: Amoxicillin-clavulanate
medications.note: Finish all of the doses even if you feel better.

medications.name: Azithromycin
medications.note: Take it at the same time each day.

diet: Drink plenty of fluids, about 8 cups (2 liters) of water or other non-caffeinated drinks each day, unless told otherwise.
Eat small, regular meals. Your appetite may be low for a few days.
activity: Rest as much as you need for the first week and build up slowly. Short walks around the house are encouraged.
Do not smoke and avoid smoke from others. Return to work or school only after your follow-up visit.
care: Take 5 slow deep breaths every hour while awake to help clear your lungs.
Cough up mucus rather than suppressing it.
monitoring: Check your temperature every evening for 7 days and write it down.
Notice whether your cough and breathing are getting better each day.

follow_up.purpose: a repeat chest X-ray to make sure the pneumonia has cleared

warning_signs: severe trouble breathing or you cannot speak a full sentence
call_clinic: a fever of 101 F (38.3 C) or higher after 3 days of antibiotics
your cough or shortness of breath is getting worse
you cannot keep your antibiotics down
